A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dimension data of H is a local invariant of H (relative to its embedding in G), but is not a global one.
we have shown that \emph{local} conjugacy is not enough to ensure global conjugacy, even for simple H.
we have provided a unified treatment for these disconnected and disconnected cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local-global correspondence is not always multiplicity free.
one can prove local results (in the sense of local Langlands correspondence) by studying local conjugacy of pairs of embeddings of H in G.
one should be able to produce such examples for arbitrary G and H, by using the Langlands classification and the theory of endoscopy.
